absent: Semantics of hardware invalidation primitives and global synchronization.
Definitions of secondary control accessors, intercept helpers, activity checks and lapic helpers.
Posted descriptor memory layout beyond pending state and notification vector selection.
User return setup, guest host mask construction, enclave bitmap format and exception update rules.
CPUID lookup failure handling, trace validation rules and transactional encodings.
Segment rights encoding beyond size indicators, descriptor limit semantics and debug reserved bits.
Sleep contexts and lock ordering beyond the VMCS guard and virtual CPU mutex requirement.
Trust domain detection, descriptor initialization and trace payloads.
Outer control allocation lifetime and nested guest host validation predicates.
Feature control valid bit meanings and physical width handling in fault interception.

findings.text: Public helpers in these fragments offer EPT context synchronization, virtual APIC in service update, posted to request synchronization, standard and trust domain interrupt delivery, post CPUID refresh, segment and privilege queries, control register validation, descriptor table and debug register access, plus nested control validity checks.

Interrupt related VT entry points first test for a trust domain virtual CPU. Hardware in service updates and posted synchronization return early with neutral results for such guests and otherwise delegate to VMX helpers, while delivery diverts trust domain guests to a posted only trust domain helper and ordinary guests to the VMX delivery helper.

State query VT entry points isolate trust domain guests by returning zeroed structures or zero values and skipping VMX work, while ordinary guests delegate to the matching VMX helper for post CPUID refresh, exception bitmap refresh, segment base and segment access, privilege level with and without cache, and code size attributes.

Control and table VT entry points apply the same isolation. Trust domain guests report control values as valid, ignore control and table writes, return zeroed descriptor tables, and report success for extended feature writes, while ordinary guests delegate validation and access for control registers, feature register, interrupt and global descriptor tables and debug control to VMX helpers.

Maintains a cached bitmap mode per virtual CPU for x2APIC operation. It derives the desired mode from whether virtualized x2APIC control is active and whether APIC virtualization is enabled and active, leaves the bitmap untouched when the cached mode already matches, otherwise stores the new mode and rebuilds read and write portions for the emulated range while keeping higher extended registers intercepted, then adjusts interception for task priority always and for end of interrupt, self delivery and interrupt command conditionally under full virtualization. Operation is skipped without the required bitmap hardware or without an in kernel LAPIC.

Synchronizing posted interrupts first drains the posted notification flag with ordering and merges posted pending bits into LAPIC request state when present, otherwise inspects the current highest request. When the virtual CPU is outside guest mode and APIC virtualization is active it refreshes the requested interrupt hint. Otherwise it requests event processing only when the highest pending request originated from the posted set, avoiding repeated wakeups for blocked interrupts.

General posted delivery tries nested handling first, then requires active APIC virtualization before posting to the per virtual CPU descriptor. On posted failure the caller materializes the interrupt in the in kernel LAPIC request set, requests event processing and kicks the virtual CPU, while successful posting only records acceptance for tracing.

After guest CPUID is updated the implementation clears extended save features when the base feature is absent, rebuilds user return MSRs, refreshes secondary execution controls when supported, adjusts feature control validity for nested virtualization and enclave features, updates nested fixed control bits when virtualization is exposed, refreshes processor trace configuration when supported by host and guest, conditions transactional control on guest exposure, rebuilds guest host masking, rewrites the enclave exit bitmap, and finally refreshes exception interception to account for physical address width changes.

Nested posted interrupt delivery succeeds only when the virtual CPU is in guest mode and the target vector equals the cached posted notification vector from the outer hypervisor, in which case it marks a nested pending flag, requests event processing, orders the request against mode checks, and triggers the nested notification vector. Otherwise it reports failure so the caller falls back to other paths, deliberately avoiding direct use of outer control state.

Rewriting secondary execution controls preserves a fixed set of dynamic bits related to shadow control structures, virtualized x2APIC mode, virtualized APIC accesses and descriptor handling, merging retained current bits with newly requested non dynamic bits.

Nested fixed one bits start from all ones for the first control register and a performance counter baseline for the fourth, then selectively enable additional fourth register allowances according to guest feature presence across basic, structured extended and additional leaves, covering virtualization, memory protection, paging and security extensions.

Processor trace guest configuration copies the full set of trace CPUID leaves into the per virtual CPU descriptor, derives the count of configurable address ranges, starts from a mask that denies all independent controls, then selectively permits individual controls such as address filtering, cycle, timing, write tracing, power events, table output, fabric output and per range controls only when the corresponding capability is present.

Reading a segment base returns an emulated segment value when virtual 8086 mode is active and otherwise reads the hardware cached guest segment base directly. Writing a segment updates the underlying guest segment state and then re evaluates whether instruction emulation is required, storing the result in the common emulation flag.
Privilege level queries delegate to a common helper, with the no cache variant bypassing cached state.
First control register validation depends on nesting state. Guests in nested operation use nested guest rules, hosts with nesting enabled use nested host rules, otherwise any value is accepted.

Fourth control register validation rejects enabling virtual machine extensions under system management mode and, when nesting is enabled, additionally requires nested fixed bit and common validity checks. The nested check combines fixed zero and fixed one constraints with the common fourth register validity predicate.

Guest descriptor table state is accessed as paired limit and base fields with matching read and write operations for interrupt and global tables, while debug control is written as a single guest value.
Trust domain interrupt delivery supports only the posted mechanism and performs no local APIC emulation, posting the vector into the trust domain descriptor and recording acceptance.
EPT synchronization prefers a context scoped hardware invalidation when the processor reports support and otherwise falls back to a global synchronization for the supplied pointer.

Updating the hardware virtual APIC in service state requires holding the first VMCS context guard while reading and conditionally rewriting the guest interrupt status field, ensuring the correct control structure is current during the update.
Outer nested control state has lifetime tied to a lock, so fast paths avoid touching it and use cached values instead.

Observed per virtual CPU state includes a posted descriptor with pending bitmap and notification flag, a cached x2APIC bitmap mode with a pointer to bitmap storage, nested posted state with cached notification vector and pending flag, nested control register fixed values, a processor trace descriptor with capability words, control mask and range count, a real mode active flag, and an emulation required flag.

Because an external DMA agent may set the notification flag, the clear path orders memory even in single CPU configurations. Nested posted delivery adds further ordering to make the event request visible relative to the subsequent guest mode check, pairing with entry path ordering.

Requesting event processing for any pending interrupt risks an infinite loop when the interrupt is blocked and remains pending until a window opens, so the implementation requests processing only when the highest pending vector originated from the posted set. Cases where lower priority posted bits merge beneath an already higher pending vector intentionally skip the request because delivery will be re evaluated on next interception or nested exit.

Synchronizing posted interrupts while global APIC virtualization is disabled is treated as a host bug and fails, while attempting bitmap updates without the required hardware support is ignored, with a one time warning when the LAPIC is not in kernel.
Emulation covers APIC range up to 0x3f0, mapped to MSR 0x83f, with dynamic bitmap updates confined to MSRs 0x800 to 0x83f and 64 bits. MSRs 0x840 and above remain intercepted.

Guest interrupt status carries requested virtual interrupt in the low byte and supervisor virtual interrupt in the high byte. Callers normalize a missing vector value of negative one to zero before comparing and update only on change.
Code segment access rights encode long mode indicator in bit 13 and default size indicator in bit 14.
Nested fourth register allowances are derived from CPUID leaf 0x1 and leaf 0x7 subleaves 0 and 1, while processor trace capabilities are copied from CPUID leaf 0x14 across its subleaves.
